title: Lute Village’s Disciple
text: “Well then, I say I shall go speak with him.”
And so I went to have a word with Panda’s foster father, but it seemed he was in the middle of talking with some customer.
“Oh my. What’s the matter?”
“Kou wanted to go to that village over there, so I came to ask if we should give it a lift, I say.”
“Hmm… what should we do, I wonder…”
Panda’s foster father seemed to be pondering, looking somewhat troubled.
“What seems to be the matter?”

“Ah, probably because I’ve been running stalls around here so often, old customers keep calling out to me. So I’ve been asked if I wouldn’t go teach some tricks of the trade to some disciples. Apparently there’s money in it too.”

Hmm… Panda’s foster father was supposed to be running stalls alongside Father, in the capacity of Panda’s chaperone. Whether it was really acceptable to go rake in a fortune here was a rather troubling question, I say.
“Why would such a request come to you, I wonder?”
“With the Waves stirring up fears of famine, it seems they want to make even foods people don’t normally eat into something delicious, so it can be served properly.”
“The Bioplants are already being spread from Lazy Pig’s house, so shouldn’t that be enough, I say?”
“Just that alone, people get tired of it.”

Panda’s foster father’s reasoning wasn’t entirely without merit, I say. Even the Filolial-samas grew tired of eating nothing but monster meat, so we made sure to offer a variety of things for them to eat. Father apparently once said that Filolial-samas would eat anything with legs except chairs and tables, but that wasn’t quite true, I say.
“There’s apparently a disciple in the nearby village of Lute who failed some test once, so they asked if I’d go lend a hand, discreetly.”
Hmm…? Was there such an event? I don’t believe anything like that had happened before… no, wait, I feel like I’ve glimpsed it somewhere in the corner of my memory.
“I have a feeling it’ll probably be fine, I say. As it happens, Father is currently in that very village. It might already be resolved before we even get there, I say.”
“Ah, I see. If Shield Hero-sama is there, then surely there’s nothing to worry about. If he hasn’t gotten involved, I’ll go help out later. Well then, I’ll pass that along.”

Panda’s foster father knew well enough of Father’s cooking skills, I say. He often cooked together with him, much to the Filolial-samas’ delight. And so Panda’s foster father decided to set the matter of Lute Village aside for later, and instead return to Panda’s village together with Kou and the others for the time being.
“Well then, let’s go~”
“Kitamura-dono.”
Just as we were getting ready, Éclair and Crocodile Man called out to us for some reason.
“What is it, I wonder? Aren’t you two resting?”
“I’ve rested enough for now. My vitality is recovering thanks to the magical healing as well, so I’m on the mend.”
Hmm… it seemed she’d recovered fairly well in just a day. But there was still some lingering fatigue visible, which was probably why Crocodile Man was worried.
“As a bit of light exercise, if there’s nothing else planned, might I go see my father’s territory? Wasn’t there talk of a fast-footed Filolial? Would you lend her to us?”
“Is there any Filolial-sama who’d like to go along, I wonder?”
“We get to run? I wanna go!”

And so a few Filolial-samas raised their hands, I say. So Éclair and the others were off to check on the place. Now then… what should I do today, I wonder? Should I tag along with Kou and play in Panda’s village, or go along with the Filolial-sama accompanying Éclair and the others?
“Kitamura, Kou’s gonna play with Elmelo and Uncle and everyone else, so you can come later~”
Kou raised a hand here, I say.
“Understood. Well then, Kou, I leave everyone in your care, I say.”
“Yay~! Kou’s gonna study lots of things with Elmelo, together with Raph and Rifana! We’re gonna sing fun songs and laugh together with everyone~”
“Fufu… well then, I’ll go on ahead.”
“Well then, take care, I say.”
And so I sent Kou and the others flying off through the Portal.
“Well then, since I’m worried about Éclair and Crocodile Man, and also have nothing else to do, I’ll tag along, I say.”
“Is it really necessary to state so bluntly that you have nothing else to do?”
“I don’t think you need to go that far, but… well, I suppose it can’t be helped?”
“Let’s go~! Well then, we’re off!”

And so, changing our plans somewhat, we decided to head to Éclair’s childhood home, located next to Big Sister’s village—the very land that was destined to become Father’s territory in the future. Even so… the dream I’d seen last night was weighing on my mind something fierce, I say. I could only pray that nothing ominous would come to pass.
“Take care!”
“Rabbit Man, tomorrow you’re to act according to plan, I say.”
I made sure to nail that point firmly into Rabbit Man as he saw us off, I say.
“I really wish you wouldn’t saddle me with these strange duties on your own whim…”
“If you run away, that’s guilty, I say. No matter what, you’re doing it, I say.”

Otherwise, we’d have to ask the likes of Lazy Pig to do it, and that would be a dissatisfaction of the highest order, I say. Even today, she’s turned the trapeze netting into a hammock and is out cold asleep in it.
“Even if you enjoy handing out these odd duties so much…”
“Think of it as payback for teaching you how to get Father to like you, I say.”
“I haven’t even had time to put it into practice, though.”

Ugh, his hair-splitting was awfully noisy, I say. Should I turn you into a Pioneer Fairy too, I wonder! No, wait, he’d probably be delighted by that, so no good, I say. In any case, thus did we set off, one path leading straight toward Éclair’s former territory, I say.
“Ugh…”
“Are you all right, Éclair-sama?”
By the time Éclair had drawn near the destination, she’d gone pale from the noble bout of motion sickness brought on by the Filolial-sama’s ride.
“I—I’m fine. But… I should be at least somewhat used to riding by now, so why am I getting this motion sick…”
“I got sick too, at first. Everyone gets sick at first. There’s nothing to do but get used to it.”
“Hmm… I would like to build up a tolerance little by little.”

Not yet fully recovered, Éclair nonetheless made her way on foot the rest of the way, and we arrived at the ruined town that was once her territory. Ah, how nostalgic, I say. This was the very town that, in the first world, was said to have been rebuilt by Fiancée—Éclair’s territory. If, hypothetically—if Father had chosen Crocodile Man as his very first slave, this might have been the place that became Father’s territory instead, I say. As I walked through the ruined town, I found myself recalling the rather adult Filo-tan from that route where only Crocodile Man had been chosen. The scars of the Waves’ damage remained here, just as in Big Sister’s village. In one corner of that town, Éclair stopped and stared down at the ground.
“Éclair-sama.”
“……Ah. This is where Father breathed his last. He stood bravely at the front, protecting the people, so they say.”
“That’s right… I was tasked with the evacuation and was away, so I wasn’t able to be there at the moment of his death.”

It was a terrible battle… Crocodile Man and Éclair both seemed to be recalling the damage wrought by the Wave. There was apparently a story that Big Sister, too, had barely managed to flee with her life. The Wave’s boss was said to have been a three-headed Dimension Cerberus. Piecing together what I’d heard… Éclair’s parents had drawn its attention and fought together in coordination, but it had proven too strong, and they’d been struck down in return. From there, it had apparently come as far as Big Sister’s village and massacred the people there. But given the strength of the Dimension Chimera, was that really the level of boss it had been, I wonder? It was a bit questionable, but… relying on game knowledge here probably wasn’t the wisest course, I say.
“Did Éclair fight, I wonder? Against the Wave’s boss?”
“I won’t bother minding you getting my name wrong this time… I wasn’t there at the scene. By the time I heard word that a Wave had struck near my father and rushed over as fast as I could…”

Hmm, so she hadn’t been able to be there in time, I say. If she’d somehow managed to be there, might Éclair’s parents have survived, I wonder? One might say there’s no end to counting up such what-ifs, but since it’s precisely because of those what-ifs that I stand here now, I think I’m entitled to ponder them a little, I say.
